$comment: Image pipeline settings shared by scripts/optimize-images.mjs (build time), src/data/slides.ts and src/config/animation.ts (runtime). Run `npm run images` after changing anything here or replacing a file in assets-src/.

geometry.$comment: Panel aspect = width/height of one panel's own share of the panorama. seam = overlap with each neighbour, as a fraction of that width; every image is cropped to aspect × (1 + seam) so its edges line up exactly with its neighbours.

harmonize.$comment: How strongly the colours and light of touching edges are pulled together (0 = off, 1 = identical average colour at the seam), and how far into the image the correction reaches (in seam widths).

strips.$comment: A strip is one continuous wide image that several panels are cut from, side by side, so the seams between those panels are pixel-identical. centerX = centre of slot 0 (fraction of the strip width); pitch = one panel's own width (fraction of the strip width, landscape only — portrait panels use the full strip height); focusY = vertical crop position.

smart-home.$comment: focus = where the landscape crop sits (0–1, as object-position); zoom = that crop this many times closer — here on the control panel, so the panel as seen (turned with the wall) is in the middle of the card; portraitFocusX does the same on phones.

screen.$comment: Where the live control screen (src/components/SmartHome) sits on the wall, in source-image pixels, before tilting: the photo only has dark glass there. tilt = the panel turned with the wall about the screen's left edge (degrees), perspective = viewing distance in source px — the photo was composited with this projection and the CSS transform of the screen repeats it.

pages.$comment: Photos of the stand-alone pages (smart-home/…), encoded as they are (no grade, no seams): the landscape view (crop = left, top, width, height of the source, when not the whole photo) and a crop for phones. All positions in source-image pixels. panel = corners of the screen glass (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left), where the live control screen is laid over the photo; window = left and right edge of the glass façade the curtain draws across. extras = further images of a page (camera feeds, the drawing of a view, light variants…): each one cut from its own source (crop = left, top, width, height) and encoded at its widths as <name>-<w>.avif / .webp.
